Trading in Lane

Learn when to hit your opponent, when to back off, and how to come out ahead in every exchange of damage.

What a trade is

A trade is any exchange of damage between you and your lane opponent. If you deal more damage than you take, you won the trade. Win enough trades and your opponent has to recall, lose farm, or die. Lose them and the same happens to you.

Trades come in two sizes:

  • Short trades: hit your opponent with an ability or a few attacks, then walk away before they can answer. Most laning is short trades.
  • All-ins: use everything (abilities, ultimate, summoner spells like Ignite) to try to kill. Only do this when your damage plus theirs says you'll win.

Minion aggro: the hidden damage

When you attack an enemy champion while you're near their minions, those minions switch to attacking you. Early in the game, a full wave of minions deals a surprising amount of damage. Many trades are lost not because of the opponent, but because five minions joined in.

  • Trade when the enemy wave is small or when you're standing away from their minions.
  • After you hit your opponent, step back out of minion range. Minion aggro only lasts a couple of seconds.
  • Your own minions help too: trade when your wave is bigger, and the enemy will get hit by your minions instead.
Common mistakeWalking into a big enemy wave to chase a trade. You'll take damage from every minion, and the enemy just has to stand there and fight back.

When to trade

The best time to trade is when your opponent can't hit back. Look for these moments:

  • They just used an important ability. If Ahri misses her Charm, she has no way to stop you for about 12 seconds. Walk forward and punish.
  • They go for a last hit. When your opponent attacks a minion, they can't attack you for a moment, and they're often standing forward. This is the most common trade timing.
  • You hit a level spike first. Reaching level 2 or 3 before your opponent gives you one more ability. That's a big advantage for a few seconds.
  • Your ability is up and theirs isn't. Track cooldowns. See Matchups, Cooldowns & Lane Priority.
Pro tipWatch your opponent's attack animation on minions. The moment they commit to a last hit, throw your ability. They either take the damage or miss the minion, and both are good for you.

Level 2 and level 3 spikes

Level 2 is the first big spike of the game. In a solo lane, you hit level 2 after the first full wave plus one melee minion of the second wave. In bot lane, where experience is split, it takes the first wave plus three minions of the second.

Whoever gets level 2 first can often win a trade for free. Push the first wave a little faster (hit minions with attacks, not just last hits), and when the level-up sound plays, walk forward and use your new ability before your opponent catches up.

Level 3 brings a third ability, which unlocks full combos for most champions. Level 6 is the biggest early spike because of your ultimate. If your opponent is level 6 and you're not, play safe until you catch up.

Using brush

Each lane has bushes (brush) on the sides. When you stand in a brush, enemies can't see you unless they have vision there. That gives you two advantages:

  • Minions don't aggro on you as easily if the enemy can't see you hit them first.
  • Your opponent can't see your position, so they can't aim skill shots well, and they don't know when you'll attack.

In bot lane especially, controlling the brush is huge. If the enemy support is standing in your brush, it's dangerous to walk up. Use a ward or your trinket to check brush before walking in, and use the brush yourself to hide before a trade.

Judging the trade

After every trade, ask yourself three questions:

  1. Who lost more health? Count percentages, not raw numbers.
  2. Who lost more farm? A trade where you deal 20% more damage but miss two cannon minions might not be worth it.
  3. What's on cooldown now? If you used everything and they still have their combo, step back and wait.

Over time you'll learn each matchup's rhythm. Some champions want to trade constantly (like Draven or Caitlyn with their long range or strong early damage), while others want to farm safely and scale (like Veigar).

Key takeaways

  • Trade when your opponent can't hit back: after they use a key ability or while they last-hit.
  • Minion aggro is real damage. Don't trade inside a big enemy wave.
  • Getting level 2 or 3 first gives you a free window to trade.
  • Use brush to hide your position and avoid minion aggro.
  • Judge a trade by health, farm and cooldowns, not just damage dealt.
